utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Groome.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. I wanted to address the Court on the issue of another witness VG-42 and it is a matter that directly affects our ability to meet our burden of proof on count 6 and 7 of the indictment, the murder of seven Bosnian Muslim men at the Varda factory. There has already been a great deal of time devoted both in pleadings and in decisions regarding VG-42, most of it arising out of a pre-trial matter. Although the Prosecution identified the witness at the time designated by Rule 65 ter, we had not made the decision to call witness by the time Judge Thelin had ruled all Rule 66 disclosure be completed at times several months earlier. It was his view that despite the absence of any violation of Rule 65 ter by the Prosecution, its failure to identify and disclose the witness according to the work plan he established was a sanctionable act and left it to this Trial Chamber to decide whether or not to permit the calling of this witness. The Trial Chamber on the 8th of July, 2008, denied the Prosecution motion to include VG-42 on the witness list, citing the failure to disclose this witness's statement at the time designated by Judge Thelin. In denying this witness the Chamber acknowledged that the evidence of this witness was prima facie relevant but held the view that the evidence was cumulative of witnesses already included on the witness list. My submission today is an effort to make clear to the Trial Chamber that the evidence of VG-42 is not cumulative and in fact our inability to call VG-42 as a witness compromises our ability to meet our burden of proof on counts 6 and 7 of the indictment. We have made this request in writing in our motion for leave to amend the witness list of the 8th of September in which the Prosecution proposed to drop another witness to this event, a witness we believe may be unable to sustain our burden on these counts. Your Honours, while I still disagree that the work plan deadlines somehow negated the right of the Prosecution to select its witnesses up until the time clearly designated in the Rules, I accept the sanction of the Court. I believe the Chamber in sanctioning the Prosecution intended to deny it the ability to call a witness not to make it impossible to meet its burden on a particular count. That, Your Honours, is the probable effect of the sanction. It is my position that such a severe sanction for what was never an intentional disregard of Judge Thelin's work plan but an exercise of the Prosecutor's rights under Rule 65 to select its witnesses would be an inappropriate and a miscarriage of justice. In April of this year, Your Honour, the Prosecution on its own initiative reduced the size of this case by one-third. Yesterday I moved to withdraw a witness and today I will move an additional witness that I believe is no longer necessary to establish our burden of proof. The Prosecution has endeavoured to prosecute this case in the most efficient way possible, but reducing the Prosecution case to its essential evidence means that the Chamber's decision denying the calling of a particular witness jeopardises its ability to prove its case. VG-42 is the only eyewitness to the Varda executions who knew Milan Lukic from before the event and saw him pull the trigger and kill the men on that day. She went to the killing site afterward and helped bury some of the victims. The Defence have been in possession of VG-42's relatively brief statement for approximately six months now, so I am requesting that the Chamber give serious consideration to our application to substitute this witness, VG-42, for Witness VG-85. In doing so, the Chamber still sanctions the Prosecution for the perceived non-compliance with Judge Thelin's work plan in an appropriate way and does not compromise the Prosecution's ability to prove its case. If the Chamber grants this relief, I would also be seeking to withdraw an additional witness who I believe would not any longer be necessary to the establishment of charges with respect to counts 6 and 7. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll consider you application and give a ruling as quickly as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And Ms. Marcus would like to address the Chamber on a disclosure matter with respect to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Just a minute.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, just for the record, the time for our response to that motion to substitute witnesses hasn't expired yet and so that was one of the things we wanted to point out in terms of you making your ruling and of course that does, I know, complicate the scheduling of the witnesses but this was just filed September 8th to substitute the witness in again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: If we were to allow the application, to grant it, when do you -- would you propose to call this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, one of the problems that we're facing now is that many of the remaining witnesses are subject to pending applications. We would like to call this witness next week. There are other pending applications before the Chamber. One of the suggestions I was going to put forward to the Chamber, I anticipate we may finish early tomorrow with the evidence. I was going suggest to the Chamber to consider devoting the remainder of the time to perhaps dealing with some of these pending applications orally. Again as I say, many of the witness that is we're trying to schedule in the remaining two weeks of the Prosecution case are subject to pending applications and after we receive a decision by the Chamber they are of course many arrangements that need to be made before the witness actually appears.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The response would be due on the 22nd if --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Monday. Monday, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Monday.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid and Mr. Cepic, would you be able to provide a response to this motion by tomorrow?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We would make effort if ordered by the Court. We'd prefer not to, of course, but, you know, it would be at the Court's discretion on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We'll try to do our best and complete this motion --

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And if we --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: -- tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: If we could just limit our response just to 42 and give us leave to supplement the response for the remaining witnesses requested by the Prosecution by Monday, that might be a fair way to split the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we can do that. We could do that. So I would expect you to respond tomorrow. This is an informal way of dealing with applications that run into the kind of problem that the Prosecution has, and the same facility will be extended to the Defence when it presents its case. Not that I'm inviting it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: I hope so, Judge. I'll be probably asking at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Ms. Marcus.

utterances.speaker: MS. MARCUS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, could I request closed session -- private session for this submission.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of September, 2008, at 8.50 a.m.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.01 p.m.,
